suspicions.claim: The basic auth error handler now returns 'name' instead of 'message' in the JSON error response, breaking the documented error format.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/tokens with invalid Basic Auth credentials (e.g., Authorization: Basic invalid). Read the JSON response body and verify the error object contains 'name' instead of 'message'.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s1 POST /api/tokens with invalid Basic Auth returned 401; base body had 'message' field, head body has 'name' field instead

suspicions.claim: The basic auth error handler still returns the 'WWW-Authenticate': 'Form' header but the error body format changed, potentially breaking clients expecting the documented error format with that header.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/tokens with invalid Basic Auth credentials. Check response headers for 'WWW-Authenticate': 'Form' and response body for 'name' instead of 'message'.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s2 POST /api/tokens with invalid Basic Auth returned 401; base body had 'message' field, head body has 'name' field instead

suspicions.claim: The token auth error handler now returns 'name' instead of 'message' in the JSON error response, breaking the documented error format for token authentication failures.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users with an invalid or missing Bearer token (Authorization: Bearer invalid). Read the JSON response body and verify the error object contains 'name' instead of 'message'.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s3 GET /api/users with invalid Bearer token returned 401; base body had 'message' field, head body has 'name' field instead

suspicions.claim: The token auth error handler no longer returns the 'WWW-Authenticate' header that the basic auth handler returns, creating an inconsistency between auth error responses.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users with an invalid Bearer token. Check response headers for absence of 'WWW-Authenticate' header and response body for 'name' instead of 'message'.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s4 GET /api/users with invalid Bearer token returned 401; base body had 'message' field, head body has 'name' field instead

suspicions.claim: Both auth error handlers now return 'name' instead of 'message', breaking the documented error response format which specifies 'message' as the short error message field.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/tokens with invalid Basic Auth credentials and separately GET /api/users with invalid Bearer token. Compare both error responses to confirm both now return 'name' instead of documented 'message' field.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s5 POST /api/tokens and GET /api/users with invalid auth both returned 401; base bodies had 'message' field, head bodies have 'name' field instead
